This is an implementation task. Edit the real source code. Do not stop at analysis, suggestions, or a proposal.

=====================================
STEP 0: RESUME SAFELY (do this first, before editing anything)
=====================================
1. Run `git status` and `git log --oneline -15`. Read `git diff --stat` to see what Phases 1-3 changed.
2. Find and read what already exists: the design tokens file (shared/design.ts), the CSS primitives, the Review page (header, summary cards, trading panel, savings panel, charts), and any notes or audit the previous agent left (README, docs, comments).
3. Find the commands to typecheck, test, and build (check package.json scripts). Run them NOW to get a baseline. Record what passes and what already fails, so you can tell which failures are yours.
4. If there are uncommitted changes, create a local checkpoint commit first (`git add -A && git commit -m "checkpoint: phases 1-3"`). Never push.
5. Do NOT redo Phases 1-3. Reuse the existing tokens, primitives, and components. If something from Phases 1-3 looks wrong, fix it minimally and mention it in the final report.

=====================================
ABSOLUTE RULES (these override everything)
=====================================
- Do NOT break existing functionality. Preserve all features, routes, navigation behavior, and user data.
- Do NOT change database schema, data structures, migrations, or stored data unless truly unavoidable. If you think you must, STOP and ask me first.
- Do NOT change existing calculations or business logic (P&L, savings balance, habit and mood stats). UI code must call the existing functions/selectors. Never write a second, separate calculation for the same number.
- Do NOT hardcode or fake any data. All metrics come from real app records.
- Do NOT add any dependency. If you believe one is needed, STOP and ask me first. Use the existing charting library, or plain SVG/CSS.
- Do NOT use destructive git commands: no `reset --hard`, `checkout -- .`, `clean -f`, `stash drop`, force push, or deleting branches. Never push.
- Do NOT rewrite files wholesale or do unrelated refactoring. Make small, targeted edits.
- Do NOT hardcode colors. Use the design tokens only (CSS variables or Tailwind theme values) so light and dark themes both work.
- Do NOT claim anything was tested, built, or verified unless you actually ran the command and saw the result.
- If a change breaks tests, typecheck, or build, FIX IT or REVERT YOUR OWN last edit before moving on. Never leave the project in a broken state.
- If you are unsure how something works, read the code first. Do not guess.

=====================================
WORKING METHOD (follow for every sub-task)
=====================================
1. Read the relevant existing files first.
2. Make ONE small change.
3. Run typecheck (and tests if the area has them). Fix errors immediately.
4. Move to the next small change.
5. At the end of each phase: run typecheck + tests + build, then make a local checkpoint commit ("phase N: <summary>").
6. Move straight to the next phase. Do not wait for confirmation unless blocked.

=====================================
PHASE 4: Habits, Mood, Weekly Insights, states
=====================================
Habits panel (Review page):
- Compact 7-day activity strip showing per-day state: Completed, Incomplete, Not scheduled, Not tracked. These four states must look clearly different (not color alone; use shape/fill/opacity too).
- Show completion percentage, completed vs tracked days, and the current streak ONLY if the existing logic already supports streaks.

Mood panel:
- Average mood, number of entries, and a simple line chart (or other simple visual) of the daily trend on the existing 5-point scale.
- Never invent mood entries. Never treat a missing day as a low score; leave a gap in the line.
- Show a previous-period comparison only when both periods have data.

Weekly Insights (new compact component, below the main panels):
- Deterministic only. No AI, no external APIs, no financial advice.
- Possible insights: best trading day, worst trading day, closed trades, overall P&L; deposits, withdrawals, net savings; habit completion rate; average mood and period comparison.
- Each insight is a short sentence, shown only if real data supports it. Handle insufficient data gracefully (show fewer insights or a calm "Not enough data yet" line). No repeated information.
- Put the insight logic in a pure function (data in, array of insights out) and write unit tests for it using the project's existing test runner: normal data, empty data, one-day data, ties, only-losing week.
- Reuse existing P&L / savings / habit / mood selectors for the inputs.

Also add clear loading, empty, and error states to the panels on this page.

=====================================
PHASE 5: App-wide consistency
=====================================
- Review every other page/tool (trades, savings, habits, logbook, tasks, settings, etc.). Apply the shared design system: same card style, buttons, inputs, selects, dialogs, dropdowns, tooltips, spacing, and typography via the existing primitives.
- Sidebar and navigation: keep the existing grouped sidebar, pinning, and Ctrl/Cmd+K command palette working exactly as they do. Only adjust styling for consistency. Do NOT restructure navigation.
- Dark mode: go through every page and dialog in dark theme. Fix low contrast, invisible borders, and any hardcoded light colors. Dark mode must be intentionally designed, not just inverted. Chart colors and tooltips must be themed too.
- Theme preference must keep persisting through the existing preference mechanism.
- Search the code for hardcoded hex/rgb colors and replace them with tokens where they affect themes.

=====================================
PHASE 6: Responsive polish
=====================================
Breakpoints: below 640px mobile, 640-1023px tablet, 1024px+ desktop (adapt to the existing layout).
- Desktop: 4 KPI cards in a row when space permits; two main panels side by side; sensible max content width.
- Tablet: 2 KPI cards per row; panels adapt.
- Mobile: single column or compact KPI cards; panels stacked; charts resize; sidebar/navigation usable on narrow widths.
- No unintended horizontal overflow at any width (check 360, 768, 1024, 1440).
- Subtle interactions only: hover/active states, focus-visible rings on all interactive controls, 150-250ms transitions, and respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- Keep the Week/Month segmented control and prev/next buttons from causing layout shift when the period changes.

=====================================
PHASE 7: Quality assurance and report
=====================================
Run and record the REAL results of:
1. Typecheck
2. All existing tests plus the new insights tests
3. Production build
4. If the app can be launched, check the dev console for new errors; if you cannot launch it in your environment, say so honestly
Verify by reading code and/or running (state which): weekly vs monthly filtering, prev/next navigation, theme switching persistence, trade-detail navigation from Best/Worst trades, that numbers on the Review page match the underlying data logic (no duplicate calculations), and no horizontal overflow.
Update the README briefly with the design system (tokens location, primitives, how to add a themed component).

FINAL REPORT (concise):
- What was completed, per phase
- Files modified and new components created
- Design-system changes
- Features confirmed preserved
- Exact test / typecheck / build results (pass/fail, with counts)
- Anything NOT completed or NOT verified, stated plainly
- Any deviations from this prompt and why

import { ChevronLeft, ChevronRight } from 'lucide-react'
import type { ReactNode } from 'react'

// The one header every page uses: title, optional subtitle (with any status badge), and the primary action on the right.
export function PageHeader({ title, subtitle, children }: { title: string; subtitle?: ReactNode; children?: ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <header className="page-head">
      <div className="min-w-0">
        <h1 className="page-title">{title}</h1>
        {subtitle && <p className="page-sub">{subtitle}</p>}
      </div>
      {children && <div className="page-actions">{children}</div>}
    </header>
  )
}

// Previous / next period arrows, always the same width so the header does not jump between periods.
// `disabled` still keeps the button in place (and readable to screen readers) instead of removing it.
export function PeriodArrows({ onPrev, onNext, prevLabel, nextLabel, nextDisabled }: {
  onPrev: () => void; onNext: () => void; prevLabel: string; nextLabel: string; nextDisabled?: boolean
}) {
  return (
    <div className="flex items-center">
      <button className="arrow" onClick={onPrev} aria-label={prevLabel} title={prevLabel}><ChevronLeft size={18} aria-hidden="true" /></button>
      <button className="arrow" onClick={onNext} aria-label={nextLabel} title={nextLabel} disabled={nextDisabled}><ChevronRight size={18} aria-hidden="true" /></button>
    </div>
  )
}
